comment: The Master Security/Quality Gate (tests/security/master-security-gate.sh) as an inventory of what a Release is asked to run: docs/23_SECURITY_PRIVACY.md §11 (dependency audit, SAST, secret scan, container scan, OWASP smoke, permission E2E) plus the SBOM that docs/25_CICD_DEVOPS.md item 10 asks for. Every one of them is listed in `items`, either as covered by a named check of the gate or as absent. Read and enforced by tests/security/check-absent-manifest.py — the `absence_witness` command of each absent entry is RUN by that checker and must still come back empty, so this file cannot go stale quietly: add a Dockerfile, an SBOM generator or a SAST stage and the gate goes red until this file is updated. Absence is recorded here, never omitted. Whether an absent capability is an ACCEPTED V1 RISK is the Supervisor's written call (docs/23 §11 allows a written ADR/risk acceptance for High; Critical is not accepted in V1) — `suggested_disposition` below is the Worker's recommendation, not that call.

kinds.covered: a check of the master gate runs this today; check_ids name it and the checker proves those ids still exist in the gate's registry
kinds.absent: nothing in this tree performs it; absent_id names the detail entry below with the substitute, the cost of adding it, and the impact of not having it

required_by: docs/23_SECURITY_PRIVACY.md §11 (每个 Release 运行 dependency audit、SAST、secret scan、container scan、OWASP smoke、permission E2E)

items.note: Three ecosystems, three instruments, three separate rows: govulncheck (Go, v1.8.0), pnpm audit --audit-level=low (Node/web), uv audit (Python adapter). Each row is red on its own and each one is NOT ASKED — never silently green — on a host that lacks its tool.

internal/config.ScanRepoExampleFiles over every committed *.env.example in the tree, with the detector's own planted-secret failing mode (TestScanRepoExampleFilesFailsOnPlantedFile) required as evidence in the same row: a scanner that stopped scanning goes red here.

tests/security/owasp-smoke.sh against the real API binary, real PostgreSQL and real Redis: the header set value for value, CORS refusals, an anonymous write as 401, the credential rate-limit boundary and the fail-closed path. It is also the G3 job `security-smoke` in specs/orchestrator/gates.json.
tests/e2e/privacy_e2e_test.go — TestE2EPrivacyNegative: the negative path is the point, so the row requires that test to have passed by name.

absent.capability: Static application security testing over the Go, TypeScript and Python sources (taint analysis, injection sinks, unsafe deserialization, missing authorization on a handler).

absence_witness.why: no SAST tool is pinned or invoked by the CI workflows
no SAST tool is pinned in any toolchain file

absent.why_absent: No SAST tool is configured anywhere in the tree: no gosec, semgrep, CodeQL, bandit or sonar stage in .github/workflows/, none pinned in go.mod, package.json or services/scientific-adapter/pyproject.toml, and ops/ci/ holds ruff and mypy configs only. CI's `go` job runs fmt/vet/staticcheck — linters with a security-adjacent subset and no security rule set, which is why they are named as a substitute and not as SAST. The absence is witnessed, not asserted: see absence_witness below, which the checker runs on every gate run.
absent.substitute_today: Behavioural negatives catch a subset of the same defect classes at the level that matters: the permission negative E2E proves a private project stays invisible, the OWASP smoke proves the header/CORS/rate-limit/anonymous-write edges, and govulncheck covers known-vulnerable dependencies. `go vet ./...` and `make staticcheck` (CI `go` job; grandfathered baseline ops/ci/staticcheck-baseline.txt) cover correctness, not security rules. None of them reads the source for an injection sink.
absent.to_add: Pick one tool that covers all three languages — semgrep with a pinned ruleset (Go + TypeScript + Python), or gosec + eslint-plugin-security + bandit as three pinned tools — then (1) add a `sast` row to tests/security/master-security-gate.sh with prerequisites and evidence, (2) decide the failing threshold (High and above block a Release; docs/23 §11 does not accept Critical in V1), (3) run it once and record the baseline, and (4) wire the row into CI, which is the Supervisor's surface (.github/workflows/** and specs/orchestrator/gates.json move together).
absent.impact: A statically visible High — an unsanitized sink, an endpoint whose authorization is missing — can land without any gate reading the source. Today's coverage is behavioural: it catches what a request can reach, not what the code could reach under another input. This is the largest of the three gaps in coverage, and the only one that no amount of running the product can close.
absent.suggested_disposition: Recommend accepting as a documented V1 risk with a written ADR, and adding semgrep (single tool, three languages, ruleset pinned by commit) as the first post-V1 security item — with the note that V1's exposure is bounded by the behavioural negatives plus the small, reviewed surface, and that this bound is an argument, not a measurement.

absent.capability: Scanning built container images for OS-package and application-layer CVEs before they are deployed.

absence_witness.why: the tree has no Dockerfile, so no application image exists to scan

absent.why_absent: Nothing in this tree builds or runs an application image: there is no Dockerfile anywhere (ops/deploy/README.md § What is missing #1; ops/runbook-steps.json release-4-image-digest). A container scanner has no artifact to scan, so this is not a tool that is missing — it is the build that is missing. The only images in play are the infrastructure ones pulled by docker-compose.yml (pgvector/pgvector:0.8.6-pg16, redis:7.4.11-alpine, quay.io/minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z, gitea/gitea:1.27.3, axllent/mailpit:v1.31.1), pinned by tag and never scanned by anything here.
absent.substitute_today: The staging template is validated statically and fail-closed: tests/acceptance/deploy-staging-smoke.sh runs 19 rules over ops/deploy/docker-compose.staging.yml, ops/deploy/staging.env.example and the nginx config, including rule R03, which refuses an image pinned by anything other than @sha256:<64 hex>. That is a rule about how an image must be referenced, not a statement about what is inside it. The dependency audits cover the application's own packages, not a base image's OS packages.
absent.to_add: First the image: a Dockerfile per application (api, web, scientific-adapter) plus a build stage in CI (docs/25 item 10). Then the scanner: trivy or grype in image mode over each built image, failing on High/Critical, with an ignore file for accepted findings; and digest pinning for every image the deployment composes, which rule R03 already demands. The scanner is a day of work once the images exist; the images are the actual project.
absent.impact: Today no deployed artifact exists, so the exposure is the infrastructure stack's upstream images and their update cadence — nobody in this repository tracks them, and a base-image CVE would be found by reading release notes, not by a gate. Once images are built, without this row a High in a base layer ships unnoticed.
absent.suggested_disposition: Recommend accepting for V1 with the gap stated plainly (there is no image to scan yet), and making the image build + trivy a single follow-up item so that the scanner cannot be split from the artifact that makes it meaningful. Nothing to scan is a reason to defer the scanner, not a reason to call the release container-safe.

absent.capability: A machine-readable software bill of materials (SPDX or CycloneDX) for each Release, bound to the Release's immutable identifiers.

absence_witness.why: no SBOM generator is invoked by the build, the CI stages or the deployment scripts
no SBOM generator is pinned in any toolchain file

absent.why_absent: docs/25_CICD_DEVOPS.md item 10 asks for a container build/SBOM stage and there is none: no syft, cyclonedx or spdx generator is configured in .github/workflows/, the Makefile, ops/ci/ or ops/deploy/, and none is pinned in go.mod, package.json or the adapter's pyproject.toml. ops/runbook-steps.json release-4-image-digest records the same gap from the release-runbook side.
absent.substitute_today: The three lockfiles ARE the component inventory in source form and they are committed and integrity-checked by the existing gates: go.sum (module graph, verified by the Go toolchain), pnpm-lock.yaml (installed with --frozen-lockfile by the web job) and services/scientific-adapter/uv.lock (uv sync --frozen / uv audit). The three dependency-audit rows read exactly those. What is missing is the artifact: a versioned document frozen into a Release, which is what an incident responder needs and what the lockfiles only imply.
absent.to_add: One generator per ecosystem — cyclonedx-gomod for Go, @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm (or pnpm equivalent) for the workspace, cyclonedx-py for the adapter (uv has no SBOM command) — emitting one merged CycloneDX document per Release, stored as a Release artifact next to the RSG snapshot hash, the Git commit SHA and the blob hashes (docs/31 Gate C: a Release is immutable and pinned). Then a master-gate row that regenerates it and fails when the committed document and the lockfiles disagree, so the SBOM cannot rot silently.
absent.impact: A Release today can state which commit, which schema version and which snapshot hash it was built from, but not which components it contains. Answering "are we affected by this CVE?" is a manual sweep of three lockfiles, and a downstream consumer has no bill of materials to attach to their own compliance story. This is the cheapest of the three gaps to close and the one whose absence is most visible to an outside reader.
absent.suggested_disposition: Recommend adding before the V1 Release rather than accepting: the generators are pinned tools, the inputs are lockfiles that already exist, and unlike SAST and the container scan this needs no new product artifact to be meaningful.
